blocked_decisions: approval roles, expiry, withdrawal mechanics and exceptions beyond high-impact separation of duties
retryable failures, attempt ceilings, timing and manual retry authority
evidence encoding details, privacy classification, retention and archival
cancellation and supersession effects on attempts and reservations beyond pending-approval invalidation and evidence preservation
budget reservation, settlement, release, refund and reconciliation semantics
commercial tier, entitlement, fair-use, quota and override values
owner_approved_decisions: One workflow per executable governed marketing-work instance.
Campaign Plan and workflow retain independent lifecycles; workflow stores immutable references to specific Campaign Plan versions and never mutates Campaign Plan state.
Approvals are immutable and bound to workflow version and action. Separation of duties applies to high-impact actions.
No automatic retries until retry ceilings and timing are separately approved.
Workflow command idempotency is scoped to tenant, brand, workflow, command kind, and caller-supplied key, using canonical request hashing.
Evidence is versioned, canonical, privacy-safe, append-only, hash-linked, sequence-ordered, and committed atomically with authority-changing state.
Cancellation and supersession are terminal transitions that preserve evidence and invalidate pending approvals.
Execution fails closed when canonical artifact persistence is unavailable.
Operator status exposes safe business state first, with technical details progressively disclosed only when authorized.
out_of_scope: provider execution, publishing, queue integration or Cloud Tasks
paid actions, autonomous agents, connectors or plugins
adaptive-rate algorithms or a new rate-limiting architecture
pricing, commercial tiers, quota values or billing
cloud, IAM, secrets, external databases, deployment or release changes
application code, tests, infrastructure or workflow implementation
scope: provider-neutral durable workflow aggregate and canonical identifier
exact Campaign Plan and optional Marketing Brief version references
ADR-0043 workflow states, failure classes and deterministic transition requirements
command idempotency and optimistic workflow version requirements
retry eligibility, attempt accounting and failure classification requirements
SQLite and PostgreSQL-compatible transactional persistence direction
provider-neutral hard-limit, adaptive-limit, entitlement and provider-budget policy inputs
